solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Heartless workers' group set up — not liked by the toffs

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are read from bottom to top
heartless means the central letter of the word for the workers' group is removed

parts.note: a union is an organisation of workers

explanation.surface: A trade union at odds with the upper classes, who sniff at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' takes the middle I from UNION, leaving UNON; 'set up' turns it upwards to give NONU.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-U was the mid-century label for speech and habits the upper class considered vulgar, so such things were frowned on by posh people.

clue.text: Switzerland is so preserved, against joining in?

indicators.note: joining in means the word for against goes inside the word for preserved

parts.note: food preserved in tins is canned
to can mean against, as in leaning a ladder to the wall

explanation.surface: A puzzled musing on whether neutral Switzerland has kept itself apart by refusing to join others.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Swiss neutrality, but the definition is about how the country is divided administratively.
explanation.definitionFit: Switzerland is divided into regional states called cantons, so it can be described as split up in that way.

clue.text: Devious when there's little support within firm

indicators.note: within means the support's word sits inside the word for devious

parts.note: devious means sly
a tee is the small peg supporting a golf ball

explanation.surface: A cynic remarks that a company turns crooked when it gets little backing from inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a company noun, but it is the adjective definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Steely describes resolve that is hard and unyielding, the same as firm determination.

clue.text: Wine transported to merchant

indicators.note: transported means the letters of to merchant are carried into a new order

explanation.surface: A consignment of wine shipped to a dealer.
explanation.definitionFit: Montrachet is a celebrated white Burgundy from a vineyard of that name.

clue.text: Ghost shortly returning after party and things we cannot name

indicators.note: after means the reversed ghost word comes behind the party word

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: returning means the shortened word for ghost is read backwards
shortly means the word for ghost loses its last letter

parts.note: a shadow can be a ghost-like presence, a spectre

explanation.surface: A spook coming back after a party, along with assorted unnameable stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ghost' is SHADOW here, not SHADE: 'shortly' cuts its last letter and 'returning' turns what remains backwards, giving ODAHS.
explanation.definitionFit: Doodahs are informal stand-ins for objects whose proper name escapes the speaker, like thingummies.

clue.text: Port taking five hundred and six deliveries?

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled

explanation.surface: A harbour handling five hundred and six shipments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deliveries' suggests goods arriving at a port, but in cricket the bowler's six balls make an over.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover is the English Channel ferry port in Kent.

clue.text: Who'd caress son struggling to reveal personal plans?

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters of who'd caress son are thrashing about into a new order

explanation.surface: Asking who would cuddle a son who is having a hard time.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from card games: laying down your hand discloses your intentions.

clue.text: Following left-winger it's hard to show old-fashioned faith

indicators.note: following means the letter for hard comes after the left-winger

parts.note: Trot is short for Trotskyist, a left-winger
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone shows their loyalty by trailing after a radical leftist.
explanation.definitionFit: Troth is an archaic word for loyalty or a pledge, as in plighting one's troth.

clue.text: Worker taken on by king, not a good person for Rex?

indicators.note: taken on by means the worker is followed by the shortened king

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker

indicators.note: not means the letter a is dropped from the king's name

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: A worker hired by a king who proves unhelpful to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Rex suggests a king, echoing 'king', but here it is a typical dog's name, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog handler trains and controls dogs, the right person for a pet called Rex.

clue.text: Curtailed welcome by relative? Anything but a welcoming word!

indicators.note: curtailed means the tail letter of the greeting is cut off

parts.note: ave is a Latin greeting, hail
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: A clipped greeting from a family member, which is in fact a rejection.
explanation.definitionFit: Avaunt is an archaic exclamation meaning go away, the opposite of a greeting.

clue.text: I must follow obvious suggestion

indicators.note: must follow means the word for I comes after the word for obvious

parts.note: overt means obvious, openly shown
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone insists on going along with the plain proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: An overtone is an implied hint or nuance beneath the surface meaning.

clue.text: Bill quickly embracing Maureen by railway

indicators.note: embracing means the word for quickly wraps round the short name

parts.note: pronto means quickly
Mo is a short form of Maureen

explanation.surface: A man named Bill hurriedly hugging Maureen beside the railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a man's name, but it is a headland, as in Portland Bill on the Dorset coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is a narrow headland, a synonym for a high point of land jutting into the sea.

clue.text: Making the most of wise words, I celebrate

parts.note: a maxim is a wise saying
to sing can mean to celebrate, as in singing someone's praises

explanation.surface: A speaker exploits proverbs and sings their praises.
explanation.definitionFit: To maximise something is to exploit it fully, getting the greatest benefit from it.

clue.text: Shaft of tool held together by end of nail

indicators.note: held together by means the final letter of nail sits inside the tool

parts.note: an axe is a tool

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of nail is taken

explanation.surface: The handle of a tool fixed by the tip of a nail.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle is the rod or spindle on which a wheel turns.

clue.text: Confused Homer, apt sadly to make literary blunder

parts.note: confused means mixed up

indicators.note: sadly means the letters of Homer and apt are badly arranged

explanation.surface: A muddled Homer, sadly given to making a writing error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confused' looks like the anagram signal for Homer, but it gives the first word; 'sadly' rearranges HOMER APT.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixed metaphor is a stylistic gaffe combining incompatible images in one figure of speech.

clue.text: Being led astray in fog, is calmer than all the others

indicators.note: in means the scrambled word goes inside the word for fog

parts.note: mist is a thin fog

indicators.note: astray means the letters of led wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wandering lost in fog is calmer than anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' scrambles LED into LDE, which goes 'in' MIST.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of mild, describing the gentlest or least agitated of a group.

clue.text: A sailor's heard in criminal acts

indicators.note: heard means the clue words are spoken and the sound gives the entry

parts.note: a salt is an old sailor, so a sailor's is a salt's

explanation.surface: A sailor is reported to be involved in crimes.
explanation.definitionFit: Assaults are attacks on a person, offences in criminal law.

clue.text: Fat should be reduced slightly — get fruit

indicators.note: reduced slightly means the word for fat loses its last letter

parts.note: plump means fat

explanation.surface: Dieting advice: overweight people should cut down a little and eat fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Example relation: the plum is one kind of stone fruit, grown on trees of the genus Prunus.

clue.text: Copper's beginning to advance in energetic case

indicators.note: in means the copper and the initial go inside the word for energetic

parts.note: active means energetic
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, plus the S of the possessive

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of advance

explanation.surface: A police officer's start to moving ahead in a lively investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman and 'case' an investigation; here they are the chemical symbol and a grammatical case.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the accusative is the case marking the direct object of a verb.

clue.text: Land suffering from arson attack?

definitions.meaning: to land, as a bird coming down from flight onto a perch
set on fire, burning, as a building torched deliberately

explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to descend and settle, and something alight is on fire.

clue.text: Hotel in very very cold French city

indicators.note: in means the hotel's letter goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: icy means very cold
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel in an extremely chilly French town.
explanation.definitionFit: Vichy is a spa town in central France, seat of the wartime collaborationist government.

clue.text: More spirited female is starting row, putting male off

indicators.note: starting means is begins the row word
putting with off means the word male is taken out of female
off, with putting, signals the removal of the letters of male

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A spirited woman starts a quarrel and puts a man off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel, but it is a line of seats; 'putting male off' takes MALE from FEMALE, leaving FE.
explanation.definitionFit: Feistier is the comparative of feisty, livelier and more combative.

clue.text: America facing new extremes of climate — period of reckoning

indicators.note: facing means America stands in front of the rest

parts.note: USA is America

indicators.note: extremes of means the first and last letters of climate

explanation.surface: The United States confronting a changed climate and a time of judgment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'period of reckoning' suggests a day of judgment, but usance is a commercial term.
explanation.definitionFit: Usance is the time allowed for payment of a foreign bill of exchange.

clue.text: My sailor is one who hunted whales

parts.note: my! as an exclamation of surprise is like ah!
AB is an able seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone proudly says their sailor was a whale hunter.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Ahab pursues the white whale in Melville's Moby-Dick.

clue.text: Fish in ditch after river's drained

indicators.note: drained means the river's letter has been taken out of the ditch

parts.note: a trench is a ditch
R is an abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A fish left in a ditch once the river water has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Tench is a freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Governor's office in state that's absorbed region to the west

indicators.note: that's absorbed means the state word takes the region word inside it

parts.note: to state is to say

indicators.note: to the west means the region word is read leftwards, backwards

parts.note: a part is a region, as in these parts

explanation.surface: A governor's post in a country that has annexed territory on its western side.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrapy was the province or office of a satrap, a governor in ancient Persia.
